issues.text: Unlisted claim, contradicted by Docker's docs: the lesson calls bind mounts a kind of volume. storage/_index.md lists 'Volume mounts' and 'Bind mounts' as separate types of storage mount; docker inspect donhang-db shows "Type":"bind" vs "Type":"volume"; docker volume ls (used in the Try-it) never lists bind mounts. A junior who reads 'both are volumes' then sees only named volumes in docker volume ls. Outline item 3 ('both are volumes in Docker's sense') carries the same error.
issues.quote: Docker offers two common kinds. ... Both are volumes in the sense of this lesson: storage that is not part of the container.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Docker offers two common ways to keep data outside the container. A named volume ... [unchanged]. A bind mount ... [unchanged]. Docker's own documentation calls only the first a volume, which is why `docker volume ls` lists `donhang_db-data` but never `/repo`; both keep data out of the container's own changes." Propose to the owner rewording outline item 3 in track.yaml to match.

issues.text: Unlisted claim, wrong as written: a named volume with the default (local) driver is also tied to one machine. volumes.md: "When you create a volume, it's stored within a directory on the Docker host." Sharing across machines needs a volume driver (volumes.md 'Share data between machines'), which depth_notes excludes. The outline only says a named volume is not tied to a specific host path.
issues.quote: The difference is that a bind mount is tied to one path on one machine, and a named volume is not.
issues.fix: Replace with: "The difference is that a bind mount is tied to one path you pick on your machine, while a named volume is found by its name and Docker decides where on disk it is kept."

issues.text: Unlisted claim, overbroad: not every volume is removed only on purpose. volumes.md: anonymous volumes "persist even if you remove the container that uses them, except if you use the `--rm` flag ... in which case the anonymous volume associated with the container is destroyed." True as written only for named volumes, which is what the lab uses.
issues.quote: The volume has its own lifecycle: it is created once, used by whichever container mounts it, and removed only when someone removes it on purpose.
issues.fix: Make it about named volumes and add it to the claims ledger: "A named volume has its own lifecycle: it is created once, used by whichever container mounts it, and removed only when someone removes it on purpose." (source: volumes.md, Remove volumes).

issues.text: Unlisted claim: Compose's volume-creation behaviour is not in the ledger (claim 5 covers only the prefix). It is correct; compose-file/volumes.md: "Running `docker compose up` creates the volume if it doesn't already exist. Otherwise, the existing volume is used".
issues.quote: Compose creates each one the first time it is needed
issues.fix: Add to claim 5 (or a new claim, kind behavior, version_key docker): "docker compose up creates a declared named volume if it does not already exist and reuses it otherwise", source_hint Compose file reference: volumes. No text change needed.

issues.text: The definition says a container always sees a volume as a folder, but the lesson counts bind mounts as volumes and its own example bind-mounts single files (schema.sql, seed.sql). storage/_index.md: "It is exposed as either a directory or an individual file in the container's filesystem."
issues.quote: a container sees it as a folder, and it stays when the container is removed.
issues.fix: If the first major is fixed (volume = named volume only), keep as is. Otherwise change to "a container sees it as a folder or a file" here and in summary line 1.

issues.text: Claim 8 is labelled kind 'opinion' with needs_verification false, but 'removing it loses the data' is behaviour. Verified here, but the ledger kind is wrong.
issues.quote: Remove the volume itself, and the data is gone with it.
issues.fix: In devops.l1.volumes.meta.json change claim 8 to kind "behavior", needs_verification true, version_key "docker", source_hint "Docker docs: volumes (Back up, restore, or migrate data volumes)".
